svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "A kidney cut in half lengthways (coronal section)."], [1, "Blood arrives in the renal artery and branches between the pyramids to the cortex."], [4.5, "In the cortex, blood is filtered at the glomerulus of each nephron."], [7, "The filtrate flows through the nephron: convoluted tubules in the cortex, loop of Henle in the medulla."], [10.5, "Urine leaves the pyramid at its tip into a calyx, then the renal pelvis."], [13, "The ureter carries urine to the bladder; filtered blood leaves in the renal vein."]]
svg.title: The kidney
svg.desc: A coronal section of a kidney showing capsule, cortex, medullary pyramids, calyces, renal pelvis and ureter, the renal artery and vein, and an enlarged nephron showing where its parts lie.
svg.text: Coronal section of a human kidney (about 11 cm long); the nephron on the right is greatly enlarged.

g.data-info: A tough fibrous layer around the kidney.
Outer region: contains the glomeruli, Bowman's capsules and convoluted tubules of the nephrons. Looks granular.
Inner region made of cone-shaped pyramids, striped because of the loops of Henle and collecting ducts running through them.
Urine leaves each pyramid at its tip (papilla) into a minor calyx, then a major calyx, and collects in the funnel-shaped renal pelvis.
Carries urine from the pelvis to the bladder by peristalsis.
Brings oxygenated blood containing urea from the aorta; about a fifth of the cardiac output at rest. Branches run between the pyramids and arch along the cortex–medulla boundary.
Returns filtered blood (less urea) to the vena cava.
About a million per kidney. The renal corpuscle and convoluted tubules lie in the cortex; the loop of Henle and collecting duct dip into the medulla.
